title: Q2 rollout playbook: Dedicated commitment tiers, autoscale governance, and rollout checklist
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Context: We need a single, actionable Q2 playbook that operationalizes dedication tiers (Reserved / Hedged / Burstable), the autoscale governance matrix, and a standardized rollout checklist for both Hosted and Dedicated customers. This ticket captures the product decisions, cross-functional deliverables, and success metrics required to ship a low-friction Dedicated capacity offering with predictable autoscale behavior.

Problem statement: Current capacity and autoscale experiments are scattered across experiments, pricing, and SRE runbooks. Sales and CS are asking for a clear set of commitment tiers + predictable fallback behavior for surge scenarios. Engineering needs a prioritized, testable rollout plan and an acceptance checklist for canarying Dedicated autoscale policies without impacting latency SLOs.

Scope: Draft playbook and launch plan that includes: definition of tiers and SKU boundaries, autoscale decision matrix (when to prewarm vs. burst), canary plan and rollback criteria, cost-to-performance tradeoff guidance, telemetry dashboard specs, pricing experiment plan for hedged reserves, and ops runbook for incidents. Excludes deep kernel/runtime micro-optimizations (covered in ENG roadmaps) but requires runtime version pins and configuration knobs to be included in rollout notes.
acceptance_criteria: Tier definitions (Reserved, Hedged, Burstable) with SKU and throughput targets documented and approved by GTM
Autoscale governance matrix published with explicit triggers for prewarm, burst, and fallback policy
Canary plan executed in one region with latency SLO report and rollback procedure validated
Telemetry dashboards created (per-tier cost, token latency percentiles, queuing ratio) and accessible to SRE and CS
Pricing experiment plan for hedged reserves with control cohort defined and expected revenue/retention metrics
Operations runbook for surge incidents with on-call steps, escalation, and customer comms templates
milestones: 2026-03-21: Finalize tier SKUs and throughput targets (PM + Finance signoff)
2026-03-31: Autoscale governance matrix review w/ Eng and SRE
2026-04-10: Canary deployment in us-west with telemetry hooks enabled
2026-04-24: Pricing experiment launch for 10 pilot customers
2026-05-05: GA readiness checklist complete and launch decision meeting
tasks: PM: consolidate existing capacity experiments into canonical tier definitions and example customer mapping
Eng: add runtime version pin and autoscale flags to dedicated-deploy manifest (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4221)
SRE: build dashboards and alerting (Grafana dashboard id: 64-dedicated-autoscale) and smoke tests
Finance: model margin impact of hedged vs reserved vs burst pricing
GTM: prepare customer comms and sales FAQ for commitment tiers
Support: draft incident templates and KB for customers on Dedicated capacity
risks: Latency regression during canary could require rollback of autoscale policy, delaying launch
Overcommitting reserved SKUs could increase cost runway if forecast models are off
Insufficient telemetry granularity may prevent root-cause analysis during surge incidents
Confusion between hedged reserves and traditional reservations in pricing messaging could increase churn
metrics: Tier adoption: percentage of new Dedicated customers choosing Hedged vs Reserved vs Burstable
SLOs: p95 token latency by tier during normal and surge windows
Cost/unit: avg GPU-minutes per 1k tokens per tier
Ops MTTR: median time to restore p95 latency after surge-triggered fallback
Revenue test delta: retention lift for customers in hedged pricing cohort vs control
